summary: Round-1 MAJOR is resolved: a deterministic unit test now provably exercises the DuplicateKeyException catch block, and the race IT was hardened with post-state assertions. The minor LOW note on fail-open spurious events was also closed. Remaining deep-stub / LENIENT notes are acceptable to leave as-is. All affected classes re-run green (SubscriberStatusMachineTest 18/0, SubscriberServiceImplIT 7/0, SubscriberRateLimitIT 4/0).

resolvedFromRound1.round1: duplicateKeyException_onInsertRace_recoversAndUpdates did not reliably enter the catch block; the lookup-then-refresh branch could win on most runs, so deleting the catch block left the test green.
resolvedFromRound1.resolution: RESOLVED. New deterministic unit test SubscriberStatusMachineTest::upsertFromTelegramUpdate_onDuplicateKeyRace_reReadsAndRefreshes stubs findByProjectIdAndTelegramUserId empty-then-present and insert(any()) to throw DuplicateKeyException, forcing the catch path on every run. It asserts exactly one refresh findAndModify (any Query, any UpdateDefinition, eq(Subscriber.class)) and verify(subscriberEventRepository, never()).save(any()) — no spurious lifecycle event. Litmus confirmed against SubscriberServiceImpl lines 123-133: removing the catch(DuplicateKeyException) block lets the exception propagate and the test fails. Additionally the IT was hardened: it now filters to the single telegramUserId=300 row, asserts hasSize(1), status==ACTIVE, and registeredEventsFor(id).hasSize(1) — closing the 'AND updates' clause (one winner registered, loser wrote no second registration). Both green on re-run.

resolvedFromRound1.round1: redisDown_failsOpen_proceedsAndLogsWarn asserted persistence + WARN constant but not that the fail-open path emitted no spurious rate_limit_exceeded platform event.
resolvedFromRound1.resolution: RESOLVED. The test now adds assertThat(rateLimitEvents()).isZero() with an explanatory .as(...) — explicit proof the fail-open path returns false without emitting a platform event. Class re-runs green.

RESOLVED. Signature is now unsubscribeManual(projectId, subscriberId); production filters findById by projectId.equals(sub.getProjectId()) before the 404. New unit test unsubscribeManual_foreignProject_throws404 stubs findById to return an ACTIVE subscriber owned by PROJECT_ID, calls with 'other-project', asserts HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND and verify(subscriberEventRepository, never()).save(any()) — proving uniform 404 + no mutation. Litmus holds: dropping the projectId filter would let the mutation proceed and the never().save assertion would fail.

acceptedAsIs.note: Deep-stub brittleness on stubSubscriberUpdate() (mongoTemplate.update(Subscriber.class).matching(...).apply(...).first()). This was flagged round-1 as a robustness note, not a correctness defect. The authoritative atomicity invariant (Tag.subscriberCount $inc gated on modifiedCount>0 + exactly one event row) is covered by the load-bearing SubscriberServiceImplIT.addTag/removeTag against real Mongo, which re-ran green (7/0). The unit tests remain valid fast guards. ACCEPTABLE to leave as-is — no false-green risk while the IT is the source of truth for the atomic counter.

Class-level @MockitoSettings(strictness = Strictness.LENIENT). The new round-2 tests (onDuplicateKeyRace, foreignProject_throws404) each drive the exact stubs they declare, so the blanket LENIENT does not currently mask any dead stub. The justification (shared mocks across many per-method scenarios, deep-stub fluent chain) is reasonable. ACCEPTABLE to leave as-is — future-proofing nicety only, no current correctness or coverage impact.

litmusTest.note: The two round-1 litmus failures are now resolved. The DuplicateKey catch block is deterministically exercised by the new unit test (delete the catch → exception propagates → test fails). The atomicity invariant for addTag/removeTag is litmus-protected by the IT (real Tag.subscriberCount assertion). The new foreignProject 404 test is litmus-protected (drop the projectId filter → never().save fails).
